steps.message: Rebuilding everything on every small file touch is about incremental up-to-date checks (why targets decide their outputs are stale), not about how long MSBuild takes to parse and evaluate the project. Those are different phases: evaluation happens once per build invocation regardless of what changed, while incremental build decides -- after evaluation -- which targets actually need to re-run.

results.content: RebuildComplaint.csproj: a plain Microsoft.NET.Sdk console project targeting net8.0, no custom imports, no custom globs, no property functions.

steps.message: There's nothing in this project that would slow down evaluation itself, and that's not actually what you're describing anyway -- "rebuilds everything on every small touch" is a symptom of incorrect or missing incremental-build inputs/outputs (or a target lacking Inputs/Outputs entirely), which is a different investigation.

I'd treat this as an incremental-build question rather than an evaluation-performance one -- worth looking at which target(s) always re-run and whether they declare accurate Inputs/Outputs, rather than me trying to speed up evaluation here.
